newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's reports record profits, sees record 1997.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's reports record profits, sees record 1997.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. reported record first-quarter profits of $344.5 million Thursday, up 14 percent from $301.6 million a year ago, crediting improved U.S. results in spite of intense competition in fast food.
The Oak Brook, Ill.-based hamburger giant said its international operations were off to a slow start, but added it expects a strong year outside the United States.
McDonald's, with more than 21,000 restaurants worldwide, added it expects a record-breaking year.
Earnings per share rose 17 percent to 49 cents, a penny below the First Call service's consensus Wall Street analyst forecast. It compared with 42 cents per share a year ago.
The company said sales from all restaurants, including franchised units, rose 7 percent in the quarter to $7.83 billion from $7.31 billion a year ago.

"McDonald's global food service business delivered strong results in the first quarter," company Chairman Michael Quinlan said in a statement. "Despite the extremely competitive U.S. operating environment, we delivered impressive growth in U.S. sales and operating income, exceeding our own expectations.
"We are confident in our growth strategies and expect 1997 to be another record-breaking year," Quinlan added.
McDonald's results were underpinned by a 5 percent rise in U.S. operating income to $271.2 million. U.S. systemwide sales were up 7 percent to $3.99 billion from $3.72 billion.

U.S. same-store sales -- measuring results from units open at least a year -- were up in the first quarter compared with the prior year. That followed six consecutive quarters of U.S. same-store sales declines.
In an interview, Jack Greenberg, chairman of McDonald's U.S.A., said he expected April same-store sales in the United States also would be positive.
McDonald's U.S. first-quarter results benefited from marketing and promotions, including one tied to the board game Monopoly.
The company has launched new promotions, including Campaign 55, which features sandwiches for 55 cents, and its Beanie Baby toy giveaway in Happy Meals for children.
Greenberg said Campaign 55, which began this month with breakfast sandwiches, was meeting the company's expectations. Big Mac hamburgers for 55 cents will be offered starting April 25.

He added that the Beanie Baby giveaway may be McDonald's most successful Happy Meal promotion -- so much so the campaign may not last the expected five weeks because supplies of the miniature plush animal toys are running out.

Outside the United States, sales rose 7 percent to $3.84 billion from $3.49 billion. The results were tempered by weaker foreign currencies, McDonald's said. Weak economies abroad and severe weather in Europe also held comparable overseas sales down, McDonald's said.
Greenberg said international same-store sales were "down a little" in the first quarter. Globally, same-store sales were about flat.
James Cantalupo, president of McDonald's international operations, said, "I expect our international results to improve for the balance of the year."
McDonald's said it plans to add between 2,400 and 2,800, with more than 70 to be opened outside the United States.
McDonald's stock slipped 25 cents to $50.125 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
